title: Compatibility of normalized direct-image squares with successive restriction
statement: Fix a scheme map p:X→Y, a normalized DirectData d and n≥0. For every finite-coefficient derived object B at level n, the completed/level-(n+1) comparison at Res_(n,n+1) B, followed by restricted d.comparison_n and the target restriction compositor, equals the completed direct image of the source restriction compositor followed by the completed/level-n comparison at B. This contains neither a completed input object K nor a coefficient reduction morphism.

proof.text: Use the identity-on-sections characterizations of sfDirectImageRestrictionComparison at n and n+1 and d.sections. The inverse of a section-identity isomorphism is section-identity, as is its restriction of scalars. The inverse eqToIso maps for coefficientRestrictionComp act as identity on sections by equality induction. Equality induction also proves that applying any functor to one of these inverse equality transports gives a section identity; use this for completed direct image, avoiding any unfolding of its coefficient construction. Extensionality of module-sheaf morphisms and these five identities identify the ordinary triangle of the two completed comparisons, d.ordinary and inverse compositors. This supplies the ordinary compatibility input to the general derived-transition calculation. The concrete map endpoints are explicit and each section identity is isolated in a proved private helper. Combine the ordinary section calculation with the abstract derived triangle before specializing the coefficient sheaves, preserving shared coefficient-category interfaces.

The inverse derived restriction compositor has the required representative formula: expand its definition as inverse mapDerivedCategoryCompIso followed by mapDerivedCategoryNatIso, and use the factorization equations of these two isomorphisms. Extract the completed/finite normalization equations from sfDerivedRestrictionComparison_existsUnique and the finite/finite equation from d.normalization. Apply the proved generic derived_transition helper in the restriction-transition module with base direct image at level n, first target the completed direct image, second target level n+1, and the inverse ordinary and derived compositors as transitions. It gives cY.inv followed by restricted d.comparison.inv equal to sfComparison_n.inv followed by the completed direct image of cX.inv followed by sfComparison_(n+1). The helper derives this from normalized right-derived units, so restriction need not preserve K-injectives.

Postcompose the equation of Step 2 by restricted d.comparison.hom and cY.hom, then cancel the invertible prefix sfComparison_n.inv followed by the completed direct image of cX.inv. The resulting equality is exactly the statement. This cancellation is proved as the elementary inversePasting lemma, applied to the mapped component isomorphisms.

theorem sfDirectImageRestriction_pasting
    (d : CompactSupportProperImageTower.DirectData l E p) (n : ℕ)
    (B : normalizedDVRDerived l E X n) :
    (sfDerivedRestrictionComparison l E p (n + 1)).hom.app
          ((normalizedDVRRes l E X (Nat.le_succ n)).obj B) ≫
        (coefficientFiniteDerivedRestriction l E Y (n + 1)).map
          ((d.comparison n).hom.app B) ≫
        (compactSupportSystemRestrictionComp l E Y (Nat.le_succ n)).hom.app
          ((compactSupportLevelDirectImage l E p n).rightDerivedFunctor.obj B) =
      (sfCompletedDerivedDirectImage l E p).map
          ((compactSupportSystemRestrictionComp l E X (Nat.le_succ n)).hom.app B) ≫
        (sfDerivedRestrictionComparison l E p n).hom.app B
